citations.title: Assisted Living Programs (definition, levels, penalties)
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for licensing assisted living programs. COMAR 10.07.14 implements it.

citations.title: Assisted living manager training
citations.requirement: Manager completes an 80-hour OHCQ-approved course with an exam. Manager then completes 20 hours of continuing education every 2 years. Penalty of up to $10,000.

citations.title: Assisted living manager licensure (Board of Long-Term Care Administrators)
citations.requirement: Assisted living manager licensure is required from July 1, 2026. The interim provisional period is up to 90 days, extendable up to 30 days (§9-3A-01(b)(2) per SB 613 enacted text).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines certified medication technician, delegation of nursing tasks, Resident Assessment Tool, incident, significant change and protective device. Use these exact terms in the manual.

citations.title: License Required
citations.requirement: License is issued for a number of beds and a level of care. The license is displayed in a common-use area (§G).

citations.title: Levels of Care
citations.requirement: Level 1 (low), Level 2 (moderate) and Level 3 (high). A resident may be served only within the licensed level.

citations.title: Licensing Procedure
citations.requirement: Application, business plan and 1-year budget, and plan of correction. OHCQ may issue a provisional license. No operation before a license or provisional license is issued. An incomplete application may be closed after 180 days.

citations.title: Changes in an Assisted Living Program that Affect the Operating License
citations.requirement: Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes. Report code citations within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level. Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure. SDAT good standing is required (§H).

citations.title: Licensure Standards Waiver
citations.requirement: Written waiver request citing the regulation and hardship. OHCQ decides within 45 days of a complete request.

citations.title: Uniform Disclosure Statement
citations.requirement: Complete the Uniform Disclosure Statement on the OHCQ form. Give it free to anyone who asks and include it in marketing materials. File an amended statement within 30 days of a service change.

citations.title: Compliance Monitoring
citations.requirement: OHCQ conducts an annual on-site survey. The interval may extend to 18 months if there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction.

citations.title: Administration
citations.requirement: Written quality assurance plan. Manager and delegating nurse meet every 6 months (§A(2)(b)). QA includes an annual TB risk assessment and review of pharmacist findings.

citations.title: Staffing Plan
citations.requirement: No numeric ratio. Written staffing plan covers scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day. Staff are present whenever a resident is in the building. Awake overnight staff are required when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it. Dated schedules are kept on site for 18 months. On-site nursing is required only when ordered.

citations.title: Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Manager is age 21+ with a high school diploma and is licensed. Level 3 has added education and experience requirements. Manager needs a current background check, TB screening, MMR/varicella immunity, first aid and CPR.

citations.title: 80-Hour Assisted Living Manager Training Course
citations.requirement: Manager completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course and exam. Manager also completes 20 hours of CE every 2 years.

citations.title: Alternate Assisted Living Manager
citations.requirement: Alternate is age 21+ with 2 years of health-related experience and the .19B(1)–(7) staff qualifications. Alternate takes over when the manager is unavailable.

citations.title: Other Staff - Qualifications
citations.requirement: Age, TB/MMR/varicella evidence, background check within 30 calendar days before employment, and initial and annual training. Also first aid and CPR, delegating-nurse competency for personal care, relief staff, proof of training, and 6-hour/2-hour cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: Lists the required contents of each personnel file. Includes the criminal history records check, TB/immunity evidence, flu and COVID-19 vaccine advised, licensure, training, and an OIG exclusion list check before hire.

citations.title: Delegating Nurse
citations.requirement: Signed RN agreement and Board of Nursing delegating nurse course. RN is on site to observe each resident at least every 45 days. RN is on call at all times (or an alternate is). RN has clinical oversight, issues nursing orders and reviews the manager's assessments.

citations.title: Preadmission Requirements
citations.requirement: Resident Assessment Tool completed within 30 days before admission. Assessment is reviewed every 6 months.

citations.title: Admission Requirements
citations.requirement: No discrimination by race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, physical disability or mental disability (§A). Do not admit anyone needing more than intermittent nursing care, stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment, ventilator services, skilled monitoring with a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition (§B). Do not admit a person who is dangerous or at high risk that cannot be managed (§C). Hospice exception in §D.

citations.title: Resident-Specific Level of Care Waiver
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the chapter index. The text was not read for this deliverable. Confirm the procedure before finalizing the retention policy.

citations.title: Payment of Funds Before Admission
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the deposit rules before finalizing the fee and refund policy.

citations.title: Resident Agreement - General Requirements and Nonfinancial Content
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Use the OHCQ sample resident agreement template, which the checklist cites to .26–.27.

citations.title: Resident Agreement - Financial Content
citations.requirement: Resident agreement states financial terms. At least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase.

citations.title: Service Plan
citations.requirement: Service plan within 30 calendar days of admission. Based on the Resident Assessment Tool and nursing assessment. Full assessment within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, and at least annually. Review every 6 months. Special care needs are addressed (falls, pressure ulcers, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, catheter, ostomy, mental illness, behaviors). Resident and representative are invited to meetings.

citations.title: Resident Record
citations.requirement: Contents of the resident record. Delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission. Care notes at least weekly and on events. Record kept 5 years after discharge. Confidentiality and disposal follow HG Title 4, Subtitle 3.

citations.title: Services
citations.requirement: Three meals plus snacks daily. Menus written a week ahead, posted and kept 6 months. Dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week menu before licensure and every 3 years. Personal care services are defined at §E.

citations.title: Medication Management and Administration
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff who administer medications complete the Board of Nursing medication technician course and are certified. Self-administration assessment with quarterly delegating-nurse reassessment. Regimen review within 14 calendar days of admission. Pharmacist on-site review every 6 months for residents on 9+ medications. Delegating nurse on-site review every 45 calendar days. Storage and documentation rules. Controlled substances are counted each shift, double-locked and destroyed on site.

citations.title: Alzheimer's Special Care Unit
citations.requirement: Submit the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form and get OHCQ's written approval before operating. Awake overnight staff are mandatory (§.14E(4)).

citations.title: Incident Reports
citations.requirement: Complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge. Reports are available on premises to OHCQ. Required content and notifications. Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a resident death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program.

citations.title: Relocation and Discharge
citations.requirement: 5 calendar days' notice and consent for nonemergency relocation within the facility. 30 calendar days' notice before nonemergency discharge. Discharge planning and transfer documents. Emergency data sheet for acute transfer. Final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days. Attorney General may investigate funds abuse.

citations.title: Resident Representative
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the list of recognized representatives before finalizing.

citations.title: Resident's Rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights with rights (a)–(aa). Give it to residents and representatives before or upon admission and post it or post where it is located. Confidentiality. Work only with consent and compensation. Adult day care attendance is voluntary and its policies are disclosed in the resident agreement.

citations.title: Abuse, Neglect, and Financial Exploitation
citations.requirement: Written prohibition policies. Report within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local Department of Human Services/APS, and the manager. Up to a $1,000 penalty if not reported within 3 days. Investigate and document on site. Post reporting signs. Do not knowingly employ individuals with harmful criminal history.

citations.title: Restraints
citations.requirement: No restraint for discipline or convenience. Physician order stating purpose, type and duration. No PRN restraint orders. Reposition and toilet at least every 2 hours. Renew every 7 calendar days. Delegating nurse trains staff. Bed rails may be restraints. Notify family or representative each time. No improper chemical restraint. Hospice coordination in §H.

citations.title: Protection of a Resident's Personal Funds
citations.requirement: May manage funds only on the resident's or agent's express written request. Interest-bearing account for $300 or more. Bond, letter of credit or net assets equal to the average monthly balance (State as obligee).

citations.title: Misuse of Resident's Funds
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing.

citations.title: Approval of Burial Arrangements for Unclaimed Deceased Residents
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm the approval procedure before finalizing the death policy.

citations.title: General Physical Plant Requirements
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the maintenance policy.

citations.title: Water Supply
citations.requirement: Resident hot water is 100–120°F at the fixture, with anti-scald or mixing valves.

citations.title: Security
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the elopement and security policy.

citations.title: Assist Rails
citations.requirement: Assist rails on both sides of resident corridors for programs of 17 or more beds (.46B per the research checklist).

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness
citations.requirement: NFPA 101 and local codes. Extinguishers on each floor and in special hazard areas, serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee. Staff trained in extinguisher use initially and annually. Emergency Preparedness Packet. 72-hour continuity. Tracking system and medical fact sheet. Plan reviewed annually. Evacuation sites and transportation agreements. Staff oriented within 24 hours. Quarterly fire drills on all shifts and semiannual disaster drills on all shifts, records kept 2 years. Generator for 50+ residents.

citations.title: Smoking
citations.requirement: Written smoking policy stating whether smoking is permitted. If permitted: fire-safe rules, designated areas, no smoking where oxygen or flammables are used or stored, and resident smoking assessment and annual reassessment in the service plan.

citations.title: Common Areas, Resident Rooms, Bathrooms
citations.requirement: Common space of 35 sq ft per bed. Public restrooms and COMAR 10.15.03 food service at 17+ beds. Maximum 2 residents per room, 80/120 sq ft. 1 toilet and sink per 4 residents and 1 tub/shower per 8.

citations.title: Laundry
citations.requirement: Section number and title confirmed in the index. The text was not read. Confirm before finalizing the laundry procedures.

citations.title: Sanctions; Civil Money Penalties
citations.requirement: Sections confirmed in the index (.57 Sanctions, .58–.60 Civil Money Penalties). The text was not read. Cite only generally in compliance policy.

citations.title: Criminal Penalties
citations.requirement: Operating without a license is a criminal offense. OHCQ gives 30 days' written notice to comply where residents were not harmed.

citations.title: Waiver eligibility and cost of care
citations.requirement: Waiver resident may be charged room and board of up to $420/month. The waiver pays services only (§D).

citations.title: Requirements for assisted living waiver providers
citations.requirement: At least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime. Manager qualifications (physician, RN, LPN or 3 years of direct care). Alternate manager. Insurance if transporting residents. Cooperation with quarterly case-manager visits.

citations.title: Covered assisted living services
citations.requirement: Defines covered assisted living services under the waiver. Room and board are excluded.

citations.title: HCBOW payment procedures
citations.requirement: Payment is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate.

citations.title: Delegation of nursing functions (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medications administered by unlicensed staff must comply with this chapter (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31C and K). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Medication technician certification (Board of Nursing)
citations.requirement: Medication technician training and certification are documented in the personnel file (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.31B). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Maryland Confidentiality of Medical Records Act
citations.requirement: Resident medical records are released and disposed of as permitted by this subtitle (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.29H). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Criminal history records check
citations.requirement: Basis for the staff criminal history records check documented under COMAR 10.07.14.20I. Text not independently read.

citations.title: Immunity for good-faith reporters
citations.requirement: Civil immunity for a person who reports abuse, neglect or exploitation in good faith (cross-referenced in COMAR 10.07.14.37F). Text not independently read.

citations.title: Food service facilities
citations.requirement: Applies to programs with a licensed capacity of 17 or more beds. Smaller programs follow the basic food safety rules in COMAR 10.07.14.48 and any directive from OHCQ or local jurisdiction.

citations.title: General hospice care programs
citations.requirement: Hospice and the assisted living program each comply with their own chapter when a resident is under hospice care in the program (COMAR 10.07.14.38H). Text not independently read.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Assisted Living Manager and Alternate Manager Responsibilities
state_specifics: The Assisted Living Manager (ALM) is age 21+ with a high school diploma. From July 1, 2026 the ALM must be licensed by the Board of Long-Term Care Administrators.
The ALM completes the OHCQ-approved 80-hour course with exam, then 20 hours of CE every 2 years (HG §19-1807). The penalty is up to $10,000.
Level 3 programs require the added ALM education and experience in COMAR 10.07.14.15.
A designated alternate ALM is age 21+ with 2 years of health-related experience and the .19B(1)-(7) qualifications. The alternate takes over when the ALM is unavailable.
The manager needs a current background check, TB screening, MMR/varicella immunity, first aid and CPR. Post the ALM's Board license verification.

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Changes Affecting the License and OHCQ Surveys
state_specifics: The license names a bed count and a level of care (1, 2 or 3). Never exceed either. Display the license in a common-use area.
Do not operate before a license or provisional license is issued. Operating unlicensed is a criminal offense, with 30 days' written notice to comply where residents were not harmed.
Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes and report code citations within 7 days. Get OHCQ approval before adding beds or raising the level.
Give 60 days' notice of ownership change, relocation or closure (49 or fewer beds). Keep SDAT good standing.
OHCQ surveys at least annually, up to 18 months if there is no open plan of correction, complaint, civil money penalty or sanction. Licensure-standards waiver requests are decided within 45 days.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Keep the written policies required at the OHCQ on-site survey current and available to the surveyor.
Review the emergency and disaster plan at least annually.
Amend the Uniform Disclosure Statement within 30 days of any change in services.
Keep a version/date log and staff acknowledgment of each revision.

policies.title: Quality Assurance Plan and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Maintain a written quality assurance plan.
The ALM and delegating nurse meet every 6 months, with the meeting documented (COMAR 10.07.14.13A(2)(b)).
Include an annual TB risk assessment.
Review pharmacist findings in QA.
Review incidents, grievances and survey findings in QA, and document corrective action.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Medicaid payment is the lesser of the customary charge or the Medicaid rate (COMAR 10.09.54.22).
The waiver pays services only. Room and board are excluded from covered services and billed to the resident, up to $420/month for waiver residents.
Check the OIG exclusion list for each employee before hire and document it in the personnel file.
Sanctions and civil money penalties are in COMAR 10.07.14.57-.60 (cite generally only).

policies.title: Medicaid Community Options Waiver Participation
state_specifics: Keep at least 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime (COMAR 10.09.54.05).
The manager is a physician, RN, LPN or has 3 years of direct care. Name an alternate manager. Carry insurance if transporting residents.
Cooperate with quarterly case-manager visits.

Bill services using the MDH rate transmittal in effect (PT 04-25: $90.74/day Level II, $114.51/day Level III). Billing moved to LTSSMaryland on Oct. 1, 2026 (helpdesk 1-855-463-5877). Enroll through MPRIME, which requires an SDAT number in good standing.
Waiver residents may be charged room and board up to $420/month. Rate sheets must reflect this.

policies.title: Resident Bill of Rights, Responsibilities and Resident Representative
state_specifics: Give the Resident Bill of Rights (COMAR 10.07.14.36, rights (a)-(aa)) to the resident and representative before or upon admission. Post it or post where it is located.
Residents work only with consent and compensation.
Residents' information is kept confidential.
Residents may use a resident representative under COMAR 10.07.14.35 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).

policies.title: Complaint and Grievance Procedure
state_specifics: Written procedure for receiving, investigating, responding to and documenting complaints.
Give residents and representatives the OHCQ Assisted Living Team contact: (410) 402-8217 / (800) 492-6005.
Provide Ombudsman contact information (see RR-03).
Facility policy: no retaliation against a complainant.
Review grievance trends in the QA plan.

policies.title: Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Agency Access
state_specifics: Allow the Ombudsman and OHCQ access to residents and to records as permitted.
Post Ombudsman, area agency on aging and OHCQ contact information.
Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are reported within 24 hours to the Ombudsman or area agency on aging (see SAF-01).

policies.title: Resident Agreement, Uniform Disclosure Statement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Use the OHCQ sample resident agreement with the nonfinancial terms (.26) and financial terms (.27).
Give at least 45 calendar days' notice of a rate increase.
Give the Uniform Disclosure Statement free to anyone who asks and include it in marketing. Amend within 30 days of any service change.
Pre-admission deposit rules are in COMAR 10.07.14.25 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).
Issue the final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days of discharge.

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Manage a resident's funds only on the resident's or agent's express written request.
Hold $300 or more in an interest-bearing account.
Carry a bond, letter of credit or net assets equal to the average monthly balance (State as obligee).
The Attorney General may investigate funds abuse.
If the program does not hold funds, state so in the agreement.

policies.title: Advance Directives and Resident Preferences
state_specifics: Ask about advance directives at admission and file any copy in the resident record.
Send the directive and the emergency data sheet with the resident on acute transfer.
Staff are trained to find the directive at the time of an emergency.
Preferences are recorded in the service plan.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Resident information is confidential under the Bill of Rights.
Release and disposal of records follow HG Title 4, Subtitle 3.
Designate a privacy officer, minimum-necessary rules and a breach-response process.
Keep records locked or access-controlled.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Do not discriminate by race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, physical disability or mental disability (COMAR 10.07.14.23A).
Provide interpreter and auxiliary aid access at no cost to residents.
Provide reasonable accommodations for disability.

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Complete the Resident Assessment Tool within 30 days before admission.

Do not admit anyone needing more than intermittent nursing care, stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment, ventilator services, skilled monitoring of a fluctuating acute condition, or monitoring of an uncontrollable chronic condition (§B).
Do not admit a person who is dangerous or at high risk that cannot be managed (§C). The hospice exception is in §D.
Serve a resident only within the licensed level of care.
Give the Uniform Disclosure Statement before admission.

policies.title: Bed and Room Assignment Policy
state_specifics: No more than 2 residents per room and never more beds than the license names.
At least 80 sq ft of functional space for a single and 120 sq ft for a double, excluding closets, bathrooms and door swings.
Each bed is a real bed (no rollaway or cot). Rooms have latching doors, window shades and closet space.
Room assignment considers the Resident Assessment Tool, resident preference, roommate compatibility and the licensed level.
Record every assignment and any change on the Bed and Room Assignment Record.

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment (Resident Assessment Tool)
state_specifics: Use the OHCQ Resident Assessment Tool. Complete it within 30 days before admission and review it every 6 months.
Do a full assessment within 48 hours after a significant change or nonroutine hospitalization, and at least annually.
The delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission.
The delegating nurse reviews the manager's assessments.

policies.title: Service Plan
state_specifics: Write the service plan within 30 calendar days of admission from the Resident Assessment Tool and the nursing assessment.
Review it every 6 months.
Address special care needs: falls, pressure ulcers, diabetes, oxygen, enteral feeding, catheter, ostomy, mental illness and behaviors.
Invite the resident and representative to service plan meetings.

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Program Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Residents may remain only while their needs fall within the licensed level and the admission limits in COMAR 10.07.14.23B-C.
Hospice allows a limited exception (§D).
Resident-specific level-of-care waivers are in COMAR 10.07.14.24 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).
When needs exceed the program's level, start discharge planning and give 30 calendar days' notice for nonemergency discharge.

policies.title: Change in Resident's Accommodation Procedure
state_specifics: Give at least 5 calendar days' notice and get consent for a nonemergency relocation within the facility.
The new room meets the room-size and 2-per-room limits.
Update the bed assignment record and notify the representative.
Update the service plan if the move affects care.

policies.title: Transferring a Resident to Another Facility Procedure
state_specifics: Send an emergency data sheet for an acute transfer.
Do discharge planning and prepare transfer documents for nonacute transfers.
Notify the representative and delegating nurse at the time of transfer.
The delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission.

policies.title: Resident Discharge, Relocation and Notice Procedure
state_specifics: Give 30 calendar days' written notice before a nonemergency discharge.
Discharge planning with the resident and representative. For waiver residents, coordinate with the case manager.
Final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days.
Keep the record for 5 years after discharge.

policies.title: Resident's Request to Terminate an Agreement Procedure
state_specifics: Accept a written request from the resident or representative.
The notice period and refund terms are those in the resident agreement (.26-.27). State them in this procedure.
Hold a discharge-planning meeting and notify the representative.
Final statement, refunds and return of property within 30 calendar days.

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Complete a regimen review within 14 calendar days of admission.
A pharmacist reviews on site every 6 months for any resident on 9 or more medications, with findings documented and reviewed in QA.
Count controlled substances each shift, double-lock them and destroy them on site.
Self-administration is assessed, with quarterly delegating-nurse reassessment.
Store and document medications per COMAR 10.07.14.31.

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization (Certified Medication Technicians)
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff who administer medications complete the Board of Nursing 20-hour medication technician course and are certified.
CMTs renew every 2 years with 100 practice hours and a 4-hour update.
The delegating nurse reviews on site every 45 calendar days.
Keep training and certification proof in the personnel file.

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegating Nurse Responsibilities
state_specifics: A signed RN agreement and the Board of Nursing delegating nurse course are required.
The RN observes each resident on site at least every 45 days and is on call at all times (or an alternate is).
The RN issues nursing orders, reviews the manager's assessments and has clinical oversight.
On-site nursing is required only when the delegating nurse or a practitioner orders it.
The ALM and RN meet every 6 months.

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: A significant change prompts a full assessment within 48 hours.
Notify the delegating nurse, practitioner and representative.
Send the emergency data sheet with the resident to the hospital.
Complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge when the change results from an incident.
Chart care notes at least weekly and on events.

policies.title: Dementia, Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Special Care Unit
state_specifics: Submit the Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form and get OHCQ's written approval before operating a unit.
Awake overnight staff are mandatory on an Alzheimer's unit. No electronic-monitoring waiver.
Personal-care staff complete 6 hours of cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training within 120 days (2 hours for other staff), then 2 hours (or 1) annually.
Address behaviors in the service plan.

policies.title: Falls Prevention
state_specifics: The service plan addresses fall risk.
Complete an incident report within 24 hours of a fall.
Bed rails may be restraints (see SAF-04).
The delegating nurse reviews fall trends in QA.

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Prevention
state_specifics: The service plan addresses pressure ulcers.
Do not admit or retain a resident needing stage 3 or 4 ulcer treatment.
Reposition any resident under a restraint at least every 2 hours.
Report skin changes to the delegating nurse.

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: A hospice exception to admission limits exists in COMAR 10.07.14.23D.
The hospice and the assisted living program each comply with their own chapter (COMAR 10.07.21).
Coordinate restraint orders with the hospice (COMAR 10.07.14.38H).
Written coordination agreement and shared service plan.

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a death resulting from abuse, neglect, wandering, elopement, medication error, burns or any injury incurred at the program.
Notify the representative and practitioner.
Return property and issue a final statement within 30 calendar days.
Burial approval for unclaimed residents is in COMAR 10.07.14.41 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).
Keep the record 5 years.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Financial Exploitation Policy
state_specifics: Written policy prohibits abuse, neglect and financial exploitation.
Report within 24 hours to law enforcement, OHCQ, the Ombudsman or area agency on aging, local DSS/Adult Protective Services, and the manager.
A penalty of up to $1,000 applies if not reported within 3 days.
Investigate and document on site. Post reporting signs.
Good-faith reporters have civil immunity (HG §19-347(g)).

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Complete an incident report within 24 hours of knowledge.
Keep reports on premises, available to OHCQ.
Notify OHCQ within 24 hours of a death from an incident (see HLT-09).
Review incidents in QA.

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: A staff member is present whenever a resident is in the building or is expected back.
Awake overnight staff are mandatory in an Alzheimer's unit.
Notify OHCQ within 24 hours if an elopement leads to a death.
Use the resident tracking system.
Security rules are in COMAR 10.07.14.45 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: No restraint for discipline or convenience.
Physician order stating purpose, type and duration. No PRN restraint orders. Renew every 7 calendar days.
Reposition and toilet at least every 2 hours.
Bed rails may be restraints. The delegating nurse trains staff.
Notify the family or representative each time. No improper chemical restraint.

policies.title: Emergency and Disaster Plan
state_specifics: Keep the Emergency Preparedness Packet (evacuation, shelter in place, notification, 72-hour continuity, tracking system, medical fact sheet). Review annually.
Hold evacuation sites and transportation agreements.
Orient staff within 24 hours.
Hold semiannual disaster drills on all shifts. Keep records 2 years.
A generator is required at 50+ residents.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Comply with NFPA 101 and local codes (including Chapter 24 for one- or two-family dwellings).
Extinguishers on each floor and in special hazard areas, serviced annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee.
Train staff in extinguisher use initially and annually.
Hold quarterly fire drills on all shifts. Keep records 2 years.
Report fire or building code citations to OHCQ within 7 days.

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Complete an annual TB risk assessment in QA.
Staff have TB screening and MMR/varicella immunity.
Flu and COVID-19 vaccines are advised and documented.
Annual staff training in infection control and food safety.
Bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan.

policies.title: Smoking Policy
state_specifics: The written policy states whether smoking is permitted.
If permitted: fire-safe rules and designated areas.
No smoking where oxygen or flammables are used or stored.
Resident smoking assessment and annual reassessment recorded in the service plan.

policies.title: Visitors and Pets
state_specifics: Visitor access follows the Resident Bill of Rights.
Visitors sign in so the tracking system accounts for everyone during an emergency.
Facility policy for pets: allergies, vaccination records and exclusion from food preparation areas.
Restrictions during outbreaks are documented.

policies.title: Food Service, Menus, Therapeutic Diets and 4-Week Menu Cycle
state_specifics: Serve three meals plus snacks daily.
Write menus a week ahead, post them and keep them 6 months.
A licensed dietitian or nutritionist reviews the 4-week regular menu before licensure and at least every 3 years. Keep the written documentation.
Programs with 17+ beds also meet COMAR 10.15.03 food service rules.
Therapeutic diets follow a practitioner order and the service plan.

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Offer activities based on assessed interests in the service plan.
Resident participation is voluntary, including work (consent and compensation).
Keep a monthly activity calendar and participation notes.

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Resident hot water is 100-120°F at the fixture with anti-scald or mixing valves.
Common space is 35 sq ft per bed. Bathrooms have 1 toilet and sink per 4 residents and 1 tub/shower per 8, with privacy latches.
Programs with 17+ beds have assist rails on both sides of resident corridors.
General physical plant and laundry rules are in COMAR 10.07.14.42 and .55 (text to be confirmed before finalizing).

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Waiver programs carry insurance if they transport residents.
Maintain evacuation transportation agreements.
Staff drivers have a valid license and are included in the background check.
Account for resident absences in the tracking system.

policies.title: Adult Medical Day Care Policy
state_specifics: Resident attendance at adult medical day care is voluntary.
The policy is disclosed in the resident agreement.
Coordinate medications, schedules and transportation with the day care.
The waiver rates for W0226/W0227 assume no medical day care.

policies.title: Staffing Plan, Staffing Levels and Supervision
state_specifics: There is no numeric ratio. The written staffing plan is based on residents' needs, scheduled and unscheduled, 24 hours a day.
A staff member is present whenever a resident is in the building or expected back.
Awake overnight staff when the Resident Assessment Tool triggers it. Electronic monitoring may be waived by OHCQ, except in an Alzheimer's unit.
Keep dated schedules on site for 18 months.
Waiver programs keep 1 staff per 8 residents in the daytime.

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Criminal history records check completed within 30 calendar days before employment.
Checks also cover owners, managers and household members (application).
Check the OIG exclusion list before hire.
Do not knowingly employ individuals with a harmful criminal history.

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: Direct-care staff are 18+ (16-17 only if a CNA or in CNA training).
Annual training in fire and life safety, infection control, food safety and disaster plans. First aid every 2 years, with CPR-trained staff for 24-hour coverage.
6/2-hour cognitive impairment, mental illness and behavioral health training, then 2 (or 1) hours annually.
Non-CNA personal-care staff show competence to the delegating nurse before working alone, up to 10 days accompanied.
Keep training proof with date, content, trainer and signatures.

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: TB screening and evidence of MMR/varicella immunity for all staff.
Flu and COVID-19 vaccines are advised and documented.
The annual TB risk assessment is in QA.
Health information is kept in a confidential file.

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Each file holds the criminal history records check, TB/immunity evidence, flu/COVID-19 advisory, licensure, training and OIG exclusion check.
CMT certification is in the file.
Relief staff meet the same file requirements.
Files are available to OHCQ at the survey.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Staff may not exploit residents financially.
No gifts, loans, wills or use of resident funds.
Residents work only with consent and compensation.
Staff report suspected abuse within the 24-hour window.
Discipline is documented in the personnel file.

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep the record contents listed in COMAR 10.07.14.29.
Care notes at least weekly and on events.
Keep the record 5 years after discharge.
Release and dispose of records per HG Title 4, Subtitle 3.
Delegating nurse reassesses within 48 hours of readmission.

policies.title: Documentation Policies and Procedures (Resident Condition and Preferences)
state_specifics: Document the resident's condition and preferences in the Resident Assessment Tool and service plan, and communicate changes to staff.
Care notes at least weekly and on events.
Incident reports within 24 hours.
Delegating nurse notes at the 45-day visit and 6-month reviews.
Invite the resident and representative to service plan meetings.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Notify OHCQ immediately of application changes. Report code citations within 7 days.
Report abuse, neglect and exploitation within 24 hours.
Report a death from an incident within 24 hours.
Amend the Uniform Disclosure Statement within 30 days.
Give 60 days' notice (49 or fewer beds) of ownership change, relocation or closure.

documents.title: Application for Assisted Living Program License (Step One: Initial License Application and Attachments; Step Two: Additional Documentation; Step Three: On-Site Survey)
documents.form_number: No form number printed. The file is named APPLICATION_AL-License-04.13.2026-A.pdf (10 pages).
documents.issuer: Maryland Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ), Assisted Living Team
documents.version: Current version linked from the OHCQ Assisted Living Providers page. The file name carries the date 04.13.2026. It cites the COMAR 10.07.14 revision effective 4/28/2025.
documents.how_used: This is the only OHCQ document that lists the policies and procedures a new assisted living program must have. The list is in Step Three, 'On-Site Survey', under the surveyor's record review, item 5 (Policies and procedures) and item 6 (menu cycle). The items below are copied from it. Everything else in the packet (ownership, disclosures, attestation, site plan, permits, fire report, workers' compensation, background checks, ALM/AALM/delegating nurse credentials, business plan and budget, SDAT good standing letter) is application paperwork and is excluded.

documents.how_used: This is the regulatory basis for the policy submission. It requires an applicant for initial licensure to submit 'Policies and procedures to be implemented as designated in the application for licensure'. The regulation does not list the individual policies. The OHCQ application's Step Three list supplies them, so that list is used as the checklist.

sections: Step One: Submit Initial License Application and Attachments (Required Attachments 1-5; Change of Ownership or Relocation)
Step Three - On-Site Survey (record review items 1-6; item 5 = Policies and procedures a-l; item 6 = 4-week menu cycle)

official.notes:
The packet has no separate policy-checklist form. The policy list is the Step Three, item 5(a)-(l) list, plus the item 6 menu cycle. Sub-items are lettered a-l in the document, so IDs are written as 'Step Three, 5a' and so on.

Submission: Step One is typed (handwritten applications are returned) and is submitted through OHCQ's 'Submit a License Application' link. There is no application fee. Do not start Step Two until OHCQ says Step One is complete and reviewed. Step Two documents are sent after that. The policies and procedures are not uploaded with Step One. The surveyor reviews them on site in Step Three, after OHCQ approves Steps One and Two, and OHCQ says the review 'will include, but is not limited to' the listed documents. Keep all of them in the manual and ready at the facility. Organize the manual in the document's own order: 5a through 5l, then the 4-week menu cycle with the dietitian or nutritionist's written adequacy statement.

If the survey finds deficiencies, the program gets a Statement of Deficiencies and has 10 business days to submit a Plan of Correction. An incomplete application is administratively closed after 180 days.

Related items in the packet that are not on the policy list:
- The Resident Agreement (Step Two, item 6) is a sample template on the OHCQ website.
- The Alzheimer's Special Care Unit Disclosure Form (Step One, attachment 5) applies only if the program will operate such a unit, and it needs OHCQ written approval first.
- The Uniform Disclosure Statement (Step Two, item 5) is also a form on the OHCQ website.

Outside this packet, COMAR 10.07.14 has other substantive requirements, such as medication management (.31), emergency preparedness (.47) and staffing (.14). I did not list them because they are not in the OHCQ policy list. COMAR .47 requires the emergency plan to include an Emergency Preparedness Packet meeting C(2)-(11), according to OHCQ's FAQ. I did not retrieve the text of .47 itself. OHCQ's FAQ also says it created an informational compliance checklist that surveyors will provide during inspections, but I did not locate that checklist.
